text:
**For most people, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** Nearly every current power station already uses it, and NMC mostly survives in older or very compact units.

## Where LiFePO4 wins

- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest difference.
  - Makers rate LFP at roughly 3,000-6,000 cycles, versus about 500-1,000 for NMC. One guide's range for NMC goes up to 2,000, but the specific NMC models listed are rated 500-1,000 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
  - With daily cycling, 500 cycles lasts about 1.4 years and 3,000 cycles about 8.
  - Check what capacity the rating is "to" (70% vs 80%). A 70% claim is a weaker promise.
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells failed more mildly. One study found a peak of 259°C for LFP versus 731°C for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Another found smoke without flames for LFP, but flames from every NMC cell ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). However, LFP is not fireproof. In one overcharge test, the LFP cell reached runaway earlier, so a good battery management system matters either way. Some sites, like VoltVanguard, overstate LFP as "virtually impossible" to catch fire.
- **Cost:** One database shows a median of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Per rated cycle, LFP is far cheaper.

## Where NMC wins

NMC cells are denser, but the advantage shrinks a lot in finished products. The inverter, case, and fans weigh the same either way.

- One database found NMC stations only about 10% better in Wh per pound ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Another found about 16% ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- The "20-30% lighter" figures on some sites are cell-level numbers.
- In some same-maker comparisons, the LFP model was actually lighter per Wh than the NMC one.

## Cold weather

Don't count on LFP being much better here. Stations of both chemistries mostly refuse to charge below 32°F, and the limits depend more on the maker than the chemistry. Check the manual for your model's charge and discharge temperature ranges.

## What to do

- **Daily or frequent use (van, off-grid, solar):** Get LFP, with the highest cycle rating you can find.
- **Occasional outage backup:** Either works, because calendar aging will likely come before cycle limits. Still, LFP is the default since it's priced about the same.
- **Weight-critical carrying:** Compare specific models by Wh per pound rather than assuming NMC is lighter.
- **Already own a working NMC unit:** Keep using it.
- **Buying a new NMC unit:** Be wary if it's priced like an LFP one.

Verify "LiFePO4" or "LFP" on the spec sheet before buying. Some pages leave the chemistry unstated.
